# date_expr — GNU-coreutils-style "date input formats" grammar.
#
# A date expression is a whitespace-separated SEQUENCE of items. Each
# item either sets ABSOLUTE fields (a calendar date, a time of day, a
# timezone, an epoch stamp) or accumulates a RELATIVE offset (`+3 days`,
# `2 weeks ago`) or a weekday adjust (`next monday`). The visitor folds
# the whole sequence into one `DateItems` accumulator; `fold.ts` then
# resolves it against `now`.
#
# This mirrors how `src/calc/grammar.cpat` and `src/jq/grammar.cpat` are
# structured: regex/string leaves, `+` sequence, `|` ordered choice, `?`
# optional, `(item, sep)+` repetition. There is NO operator precedence
# here — a date expression is a flat list, so we use a flat repetition
# (`items`) instead of calc's expression-promotion.
#
# PEG ordered choice: `item`'s alternatives are listed MOST-SPECIFIC
# first so a longer form commits before a shorter prefix can match
# (e.g. an ISO datetime before a bare calendar date; a timezone-bearing
# time before a bare time).
#
# Timezones: `Z`/`UT`/`GMT`/`UTC`, the common US abbrevs, numeric
# `±HH[:]MM` offsets, AND full IANA `Area/Location` names (e.g.
# `America/New_York`, or GNU's `TZ="…"` prefix) — the latter resolved to
# a DST-correct offset at the instant via `Intl` in the folder.

# ─── Whitespace (also swallows a leading comma, e.g. "May 16, 2026") ──
ws = /(?:[ \t\n\r]+|,[ \t\n\r]*)+/

# ─── Primitive numeric leaves ───────────────────────────────────────
sign      = /[+-]/
year4     = /\d{4}/
mon2      = /\d{1,2}/
day2      = /\d{1,2}/
intNum    = /\d+/
fracSec   = /\.\d+/

# ─── Month names (long + 3-letter abbrev, case-insensitive) ─────────
# cpat regex leaves don't accept a trailing `/i` flag, so case-folding
# uses inline `(?i:...)` groups throughout this grammar.
monthName =
  /(?i:january|jan|february|feb|march|mar|april|apr|may|june|jun|july|jul|august|aug|september|sep|october|oct|november|nov|december|dec)\b/

# ─── Day-of-week names (long + abbrev, case-insensitive) ────────────
# Trailing `s` allowed for the `next 2 fridays` plural form.
dowName =
  /(?i:sunday|sun|monday|mon|tuesday|tue|wednesday|wed|thursday|thu|friday|fri|saturday|sat)s?\b/

# ─── Timezone tokens ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Named zones map to fixed offsets in the visitor. Numeric offsets
# (`Z`, `+05:00`, `-0800`) are parsed structurally.
tzNamed   = /(?i:UTC|GMT|UT|EST|EDT|CST|CDT|MST|MDT|PST|PDT)\b/
tzZulu    = /[Zz]/
tzNumeric = /[+-]\d{2}:?\d{2}/
# IANA `Area/Location` name (requires a `/`, so it never steals a bare
# word). Validated + resolved to a DST-correct offset via Intl in the
# folder; an unknown name fails the parse. Allows 3-part names
# (`America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires`) and `+`/`-` (`Etc/GMT+5`).
tzIana    = /[A-Za-z]+(?:\/[A-Za-z0-9_+-]+)+/
# Named zones / numeric offsets are distinct shapes; tzIana (has a `/`)
# is the catch-all, tried last.
tzOffset  = tzZulu | tzNumeric | tzNamed | tzIana
# GNU's `TZ="America/New_York"` prefix form (quoted or bare). Matched as
# one token; the visitor strips `TZ=` and any quotes.
tzAssign  = /(?i:TZ)=(?:"[^"]+"|\S+)/

# ─── Epoch: @SECONDS (optionally fractional) ────────────────────────
epochItem = /@\d+(?:\.\d+)?/

# ─── Time of day: HH:MM[:SS[.fff]] [am|pm] [tz] ─────────────────────
hour2     = /\d{1,2}/
min2      = /\d{2}/
sec2      = /\d{2}/
ampm      = /(?i:am|pm|a\.m\.|p\.m\.)\b/
clockSecs = ":" + sec2 + fracSec?
timeCore  = hour2 + ":" + min2 + clockSecs?
timeOfDay = timeCore + (ws? + ampm)? + (ws? + tzOffset)?

# ─── ISO 8601 combined date+time ────────────────────────────────────
isoDate     = year4 + "-" + mon2 + "-" + day2
# Date/time separator is `T`, `t`, or a single space. A trailing zone
# may be glued (`...00Z`) or space-separated (`... UTC`), so allow `ws?`.
isoDateTime = isoDate + /[Tt ]/ + timeCore + (ws? + tzOffset)?

# ─── Calendar dates (several spellings) ─────────────────────────────
# YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY/MM/DD (4-digit year leads).
dashYMD  = year4 + "-" + mon2 + "-" + day2
slashYMD = year4 + "/" + mon2 + "/" + day2
# MM/DD/YYYY (US, year trails).
slashMDY = mon2 + "/" + day2 + "/" + year4
# DD-Mon-YYYY (e.g. 16-May-2026).
dMonY    = day2 + "-" + monthName + "-" + year4
# "Month D[ ,] [YYYY]" and "D Month [YYYY]" — year optional.
monthDY  = monthName + ws + day2 + (ws + year4)?
dMonthY  = day2 + ws + monthName + (ws + year4)?

calendarDate = isoDateTime | dashYMD | slashYMD | slashMDY | dMonY | monthDY | dMonthY

# ─── Day-of-week with optional this/next/last + optional count ──────
thisKw = /(?i:this)\b/
nextKw = /(?i:next)\b/
lastKw = /(?i:last)\b/
dowKindKw = thisKw | nextKw | lastKw
# `next 2 fridays` — a count between the kind and the day name.
dowItem = (dowKindKw + ws)? + (intNum + ws)? + dowName

# ─── Relative units ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Singular/plural handled in the visitor by stem matching.
unitWord =
  /(?i:years?|yrs?|months?|fortnights?|weeks?|days?|hours?|hrs?|minutes?|mins?|seconds?|secs?)\b/
agoKw = /(?i:ago)\b/
# `[+-]?[N] UNIT [ago]` — the count is optional (`+ day` ≡ `+1 day`).
relUnitItem = (sign + ws?)? + (intNum + ws)? + unitWord + (ws + agoKw)?
# `next/last/this WEEK` etc. — kind + unit, no count.
relKindItem = dowKindKw + ws + unitWord

# ─── Bare keywords ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
nowKw       = /(?i:now)\b/
todayKw     = /(?i:today)\b/
tomorrowKw  = /(?i:tomorrow)\b/
yesterdayKw = /(?i:yesterday)\b/
noonKw      = /(?i:noon)\b/
midnightKw  = /(?i:midnight)\b/
keywordItem = nowKw | todayKw | tomorrowKw | yesterdayKw | noonKw | midnightKw

# ─── One item (ordered: most-specific / longest-prefix first) ───────
# epoch → calendar (incl. ISO datetime) → time-of-day → relative
# (kind+unit, then count+unit) → day-of-week → bare keywords.
# `relKindItem` precedes `dowItem` so `next week` is a relative item,
# not a (failed) weekday; `dowItem` precedes nothing that would steal
# `next monday`. Keywords last — they're the shortest, most ambiguous.
item =
    tzAssign
  | epochItem
  | calendarDate
  | timeOfDay
  | relKindItem
  | relUnitItem
  | dowItem
  | keywordItem

# ─── Item sequence ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
items = (item, ws)+

# ─── Top level ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
dateExpr = ws? + items + ws?
